title: LocalDataUploadService.pushAllLocalData enqueues every entity kind via a per-row awaited loop instead of a batched outbox write
why: pushAllLocalData is explicitly a one-time bulk operation ('Called once after a local-born account is upgraded to cloud... so the user's offline learning history is immediately available') yet writes to the single Drift outbox table one row at a time across 7 loops, each await-ing OutboxSyncWriteFacade._enqueue -> OutboxDao.insertOutboxRow individually. Per outbox_sync_write_facade.dart:289-292, each insert also fires its own unawaited network drain-kick. A learner with a full year of history could have hundreds of completions/streak events/ledger entries; the one-time account-conversion flow does hundreds of sequential single-row DB writes plus hundreds of concurrent drain-kick Futures where a handful of batch inserts would do, extending how long this migration keeps the DB busy and widening the exposure window for the SM-4 race described in the companion finding.
recommendation: Batch each entity kind's outbox rows via db.batch()/insertAll (build the list of OutboxCompanions first, one transaction per kind) instead of looping individually-awaited _enqueue calls; fire at most one drain-kick per pushAllLocalData call rather than one per row.
acceptance_criteria: DB-3 Rule-0 checker (audit grep for awaited per-row insert loops against the same table) reports zero hits in local_data_upload_service.dart.
Test asserting pushAllLocalData with N seeded rows of a given kind performs O(1) outbox-table statements via a batch/insertAll spy, not O(N).
